### Leadership-interview supers — VERIFIED 2026-07-30 (typo-qa localized-batch pass)
Every name below was web-verified against a public source during the 2026-07-30 review of the French-localized leader cuts. **In every case the on-screen super was RIGHT and Whisper's gold was the wrong side** — do NOT "correct" these toward the transcript (Julie Monfelt rule).

### ⚠️ FRENCH-LOCALIZED CUTS — the subtitle track is unreviewed machine translation (found 2026-07-30)
The `Batch #1 / Batch #20 - 2026` leader interviews ship as **English speech + burned-in FRENCH subtitles**. Reviewing 10 of them in one pass surfaced the same defect classes over and over; check for these FIRST on any localized SFCG cut (SKILL.md LANGUAGE GATE 3c — translation-fidelity, not word-diff):
1. **The org's core concept mistranslated.** "multi-partial / multi-partiality" came back as **"positions partielles"** (SFCG Maya) and **"équipe pluridisciplinaire"** (Palestine/Israel teaser). Canonical French is **multipartial(e) / la multipartialité**. This is the concept the Goals section calls "the whole point" — treat it as a brand term.
2. **The org name itself misspelled** — "de **Searchs**" (SFCG Maya).
3. **"the two people(s)" → "les deux personnes"** (SFCG Rami + both teasers) — reduces two peoples to two individuals in a conflict-sensitivity cut. Correct: **"les deux peuples"**.
5. **Nonsense literal renderings** — "l'agent des ressources de **Dhief**" (Chief), "une atmosphère **spatiale**" (a *space*, atmosphere), "les zones qui sont **en sécurité**" (areas that are *common*), "à quelle vitesse, **à adaptés**", "permet **de plus en plus grand** le terrain d'entente", "et **soient en phase œuvrer** pour la paix".
6. **Register flips and doubled words** — "**Tu sais**…" next to "**Vous savez**…" (Maya 2nd Part); "et pour les / **les** générations à venir" (both teasers).
7. **Sentence structure destroyed** — the thesis line "Even when it seems unattainable, peace is possible" shipped on Maya 2nd Part as **"Même lorsqu'une paix semble possible."** (a dangling subordinate clause that inverts the meaning). The Palestine/Israel teaser translates the SAME line correctly, which is how the error was proven.
**Second pass, same morning — 7 more cuts, 23 more typos (2026-07-30, 06:00–07:00 ET run).** Kim · Karishma · Keneshbek · Peshtkir · Michel · Michael · Ben V6. All 7 routed. New/confirmed classes on top of 1–7 above:

8. **The org's NAME rendered as a common noun — the single most repeated defect in the batch (now 6 distinct variants).** "Search gives me hope" → **"La recherche me donne de l'espoir."** (Kim); "Search for Common Ground" → **"la Recherche d'un terrain d'entente"** (Karishma) and → **"la recherche de terrain commun"** (Peshtkir, *in his own supered job title*). Correct: leave **Search for Common Ground** / **Search** in English, as Michael's and Ben's cuts correctly do. **In-cut proof is nearly always available** — Kim renders "pour Search for Common Ground." right at 0:05 and "La recherche" wrong at 0:32; Karishma the same. Diff a cut against itself before flagging.
10. **Meaning inversions that survive as fluent French.** "that is how we get our resilience" → **"C'est ainsi que nous leur donnons de la résilience"** (*we give THEM resilience*) — Karishma. Same class as the Maya thesis-line inversion (7).
11. **Connotation errors in conflict-sensitive lines.** "divide them through these tools" → **"les diviser grâce à ces outils"** — *grâce à* means "thanks to" and frames the division as a benefit (Peshtkir). Use *au moyen de*.
12. **The brand adjective, not just the noun.** "our world is multipartial" → **"est multipartite"** (= multi-party) while the *previous sentence* of the same cut says "la multipartialité" correctly (Keneshbek). Canonical: **multipartial(e)**.
13. **Spurious connectives / severed clauses in the FR track** — "quelqu'un de côté **quand et** ce qui pousse…" (Keneshbek), "et mais surtout", "l'approche de transformation**,** de conflit", "pour un monde meilleur, **pour des comme**" (Michel), doubled **"via les outils via les applications"** + "**aux** réseaux sociaux" for a comma list (Peshtkir).
⚠️⚠️ **NOT EVERY CUT IN THIS BATCH IS A TRANSLATION — MICHEL SPEAKS FRENCH (found 2026-07-30).** The Michel cut is the **same-language** case of LANGUAGE GATE 3c, not the translation case, and the pipeline gets it wrong: extract.sh writes `lang=en` and whisper **translates**, producing an English gold that looks exactly like the other cuts' source audio. **The tell is that the French captions are phonetic garbage rather than paraphrase** ("directeur payé de ça" ← "directeur pays de Search", "je vois comme encore un peu plus du Congo" ← "en République Démocratique du Congo"). Fix: re-transcribe forced to French — `transcribe_openai.py` has **no `--language` flag**, so call the endpoint directly (`-F file=@audio.mp3 --form-string language=fr`) — then diff the captions against *that* gold. His burned-in track is an unreviewed **French ASR pass over French audio**, which is the root cause of Atdhe's long-open "the translation isn't very clear" note. Michel's cut also carries **no name/title lower-third at all**, unlike every sibling cut — which is why his twice-raised title ask ("Country Director, Democratic Republic of Congo") keeps coming back.
**Cuts that prove the rest are fixable:** **Michael Shipler** (best in the batch — keeps the org name in English, gets *intérêts communs fondamentaux* / *autoritarisme* / *interdépendantes* right; one finding all morning) and **Ben V6** (second-best; and the editor fixed all 3 of our V5 flags verbatim inside 90 minutes). The defects are an unreviewed-MT problem, not a capability problem.
**Standing recommendation:** the localized batch needs one native-French review pass before delivery; the vertical and 16:9 versions of a cut share one subtitle file, so fixing it once fixes both.

### 🛑 ENGLISH-SUB LONGFORMS — check that the subtitle track is a REAL translation, not placeholder text (found 2026-08-11)
`Syria English Sub.mp4 (Batch #17 - 2025)` (V1, asset `9f00a05d`, 16:03, Najwa Tawil / As-Suwayda) shipped to Creative Review with **a faithful English translation only through 1:12 — from there to the end (14+ minutes) the burned-in subtitles are generic peacebuilding prose that has nothing to do with the Arabic audio.** The speaker describes sitting on the Women's Advisory Board with the UN Special Envoy's office, running relief convoys into As-Suwayda after 2011, a man carrying a weapon and the right to self-defence, and how credibility is built by action not words; the screen reads "At first, I started as a participant in one of the youth initiatives", "I want them to grow up believing that conflict is not destiny", "You realize that peacebuilding isn't just a job". **The tells, in order of cheapness:** (1) distinct subtitle lines land on a metronome (median 6.0 s apart, stdev 1.5) — real speech-synced subs are irregular; (2) content-word overlap with the audio collapses to function words after ~2 minutes (proper nouns — Najwa, Daraa, the region — match ONLY in the first 2 min); (3) no specifics of any kind for 14 minutes on a cut whose audio is full of them. **So: on any `… English Sub` deliverable, spot-check the translation at 3–4 points spread across the WHOLE runtime before passing it — the opening being right proves nothing about the rest.** The teaser siblings reviewed the same run (`Syria CGL teaser English Sub` V2, `Francis Salah English Sub` V2) are both correctly captioned end to end, so this is a per-file failure, not a batch-wide one.
⚠️ **Caption STYLE is inconsistent across these deliverables and none of them is the blue box:** the Syria longform uses white text on a semi-transparent dark bar (matches Rachel's documented pop-up preference), the Syria teaser uses yellow text with no backing, Francis uses white on a grey bar. The 2026-07-10 royal-blue `#1E6FD6` + white rule came out of the CE social lane — **open question for Atdhe: does it govern the client-delivered case-study cuts too?** Not being flagged on Frame.io until that's answered.
**Third pass, same day — the editor's turnaround round (2026-07-30, 08:00–09:30 ET run).** Six cuts came back as new versions within ~90 minutes of the morning flags: Ben V7 · Michael V3 · Michel V4 · Peshtkir V3 · Samara V5 · Rebecca V5. **The track quality jumped sharply** — Samara and Rebecca are fully clean (`no typos found`), Michel went from 9 flags to 1, and every name/title lockup ask closed. Two things to carry into the next round:
15. **⚠️ HALF-APPLIED FIXES are now the #1 defect class on this batch — check the WHOLE corrected line, not just the flagged word.** The editor works chunk-by-chunk, so a correction spanning two caption chunks gets pasted into one and dropped from the other, leaving text that is *differently* wrong: Michael V3 fixed `ces centres` → `ces intérêts communs,` but left the orphan `d'intérêt,` chunk behind it; Peshtkir V3 took our `au moyen de` and dropped the determiner, shipping `au moyen de outils`; Michel V4 fixed 8 of 9 but kept the phantom `pour des comme`. Always read the chunk BEFORE and AFTER the flagged one — the orphan lives at the join.
16. **Michel's lockup landed.** V4 now carries the batch-standard blue super `Michel Mbei / Country Director, Democratic Republic of Congo at Search for Common Ground` — his twice-raised title ask and the "What a treasure" ask are both closed. The forced-`fr` re-transcription is still required on his cuts (the pipeline still writes `lang=en` and translates).
17. **The `Rebecca` caption style now carries a semi-transparent backing bar** (Rachel Walsh Taza's documented preference) instead of V4's thin unbacked white text — this also materially improved OCR reliability on the review side. Worth making the batch default.
18. **Peshtkir's V1 music ask is still open and now has hard evidence.** The V3 mix is measurably identical to V2 (same 76.864 s runtime; mean loudness within 0.1 dB at 0-2 s / 20-30 s / 40-50 s / 60-68 s / 69-76 s music tail) — the bed was never touched. Asked for a sparser track keeping the positive tone, ducked 4-6 dB further under the VO.
**Fourth pass, same day — the second turnaround round (2026-07-30, 10:00–11:15 ET run).** Six more cuts came back as new versions: Kim V3 · Sharmila V3 · Karishma V3 · Keneshbek V3 · Michel V5 · Peshtkir V4. **Four of the six are now fully clean** (Kim, Sharmila, Michel, Peshtkir's typo pass) — every flag from the 06:00–07:00 round was taken, most of them verbatim. Carry forward:
19. **The half-applied class (15) RECURRED — it is not a one-round fluke.** Karishma V3 took `J'espère que la Recherche d'un terrain / d'entente restera` → `Search for Common Ground` into the FIRST chunk only, leaving the orphan `d'entente` on the second, so the line now reads `J'espère que Search for Common Ground d'entente restera…`. Same shape as Michael V3 and Peshtkir V3 the round before. **Read the chunk before AND after every corrected chunk, every time — this is now the single highest-yield check on a turnaround version.**
20. **NEW CLASS — English HOMOPHONE carried into the French.** Keneshbek V3: "exclusion, which is a dangerous **piece**" (element) shipped as **"une paix dangereuse"** = *a dangerous PEACE*. The MT engine picked the wrong side of a homophone the ASR could not disambiguate, and on a peacebuilding org's own leader cut it reads as calling exclusion a kind of peace — a conflict-sensitivity problem, not just a wording slip. Correct: *un élément dangereux*. **This one survived TWO prior review passes** — a defect can be a plain mistranslation and still hide in plain sight because the French reads fluently. When a French line is fluent but odd, check whether an English homophone (*piece/peace*, *stewardship/stewardess*, *sight/site*) is upstream of it.
21. **Michel's translation ask is CLOSED.** V5's forced-`fr` diff comes back clean end to end — no phantom words, `l'approche de transformation des conflits`, `dans les conflits qui les opposent.` The V1 client note "The translation isn't very clear - please review!", open since March, is resolved with evidence. His cuts still need the forced-`fr` re-transcription every time.
22. **Peshtkir's music ask is now THREE versions old with the bed never touched.** V4 measures identical to V3 (same 76.864 s runtime; mean loudness within 0.1 dB at 0-2 s / 20-30 s / 40-50 s / 60-68 s / 69-76 s tail). Re-posted once on the V4 head asset with the concrete fix, then **escalated — it needs a word with the editor, not a fourth Frame.io comment.**
23. **Sharmila's editor fixed both fragment splits by re-timing the whole sentence as ONE held block** (0-6 s and 12-20 s) rather than re-chunking. That removes the orphan risk entirely and is worth suggesting as the standard way to apply a multi-chunk correction on this batch.
**Fifth pass — the Syria teasers, 2026-08-11.** Both FR-subtitled Syria CGL teasers (vertical `5f798516` V3 + 16:9 `a472e613` V3) came back as turnarounds on 5 typo asks each. **3 of 5 landed verbatim; the other 2 are HALF-APPLIED — class 15/19 has now recurred in a THIRD separate turnaround round, and this time one of them ships WORSE than the version it "fixed".**
24. **The half-applied fix can ADD text rather than just orphan it.** The ask was `afin qu'il n'y ait aucun bagage émotionnel.` (V2 read `afin qu'il y ait` + `sans bagage émotionnel.`). The first chunk took the fix (`n'y ait` ✓) but the second chunk had the correction pasted in *on top of* the old words and now reads **`aucun sans bagage / bagage émotionnel.`** — the deleted `sans` survived AND `bagage` is doubled. Confirmed on four consecutive settled frames on the vertical and on the full frame at 13.8 s on the 16:9. V2 was wrong; V3 is wronger.
25. **The orphan can sit AFTER a sentence that is now complete.** The `C'est finalement la voie la plus durable pour construire la paix.` correction landed cleanly at 0:44 — and the old ending still runs at 0:48 (`des efforts de consolidation de la paix qui seront durables.`), so `la paix` lands twice and the cut closes on a verbless fragment. Read the chunk AFTER a corrected sentence's terminal mark, not just the chunks either side of the corrected words.
26. **A re-post of the same ask will be REFUSED by `post_typo.py` GATE C (correctly).** When only the deletion is outstanding, the remaining defect is no longer a rewording, so the note has to change shape — post it as a **`subtitles:`** note naming the chunk to delete (via `post_note.py`), not as a duplicate `typo:`.
27. **In-cut proof the FR track is the better-translated one.** The FR teasers render `Essayons toujours de nous mettre à la place de l'autre,` — the correct idiom — where the EN-sub siblings ship `Let's always put on each other's shoes,`. When two localizations of one interview disagree, diff them against each other before deciding which side is defective.
**➡️ STANDING RECOMMENDATION (escalate rather than flag a fourth time):** note 23 already has the cure — Sharmila's editor applied a multi-chunk correction by **re-timing the whole sentence as ONE held caption block** instead of re-chunking, which removes the orphan risk entirely. Make that the batch instruction for every correction on this localized batch.
**Sixth pass — the North Macedonia CGL teasers (Vilma Milchev / Mozaik), 2026-08-13.** Four deliverables landed together: the base teaser V2 (vertical `70a696d8` + 16:9 `7b62fa1a`) now carries a **FRENCH-ONLY** track, and two **new standalone `English Sub` V1s** (vertical `d24d6930` + 16:9 `2fb128b3`) carry the English. ⚠️ The 7/30 brief asked for **bilingual EN+FR in one file**; the editor delivered EN and FR as separate files instead — judgment call, reported to Atdhe, not flagged on Frame.io. Carry forward:
28. **The vertical/16:9 pair shares ONE subtitle file per language, and the EN and FR tracks share the same CHUNKING — so the same defect lands in four places.** Four English fixes (missing list comma after `language`; a period after `for our children.` severing the `so that…` clause; the comma splice `with the joint efforts, we can make the success`; missing comma after `children` in the `with parents, with children…` list) and four French fixes (`sur le visibilité` gender; `besoin de ressentir cela leurs enfants` for *sentir que*; the severed `Nous pouvons réussir.` / `de la concrétisation de cette idée.`; `les enfants Mozaik étaient jouer ensemble`) each had to be confirmed on the second asset's own crops and posted twice. Fixing one subtitle file per language closes both cuts.
29. **On 16:9 SFCG cuts the default caption-band crop CLIPS LINE 2 of a two-line caption** — `chunkseq` reported `with the language identity` with the second line missing entirely, which reads exactly like a truncated caption. Re-crop taller (`crop=iw:ih*0.45:0:ih*0.50`) before judging anything on a horizontal cut.
30. **Client asks on this line, graded 2026-08-13:** the 7/29 `"we charge the batteries" not "recharge"` ask is **ADDRESSED** (FR reads `Nous chargeons les batteries`; the EN-sub sibling reads `we charge the batteries`). The 7/29 **"more coherence for someone who doesn't know what Mozaik is" ask is still NOT ADDRESSED** — nothing in either cut defines Mozaik, the first mention lands at 0:38, and **neither cut carries a name/title lower third for Vilma at all** (same missing-lockup gap as Michel's cut, note 16). Posted as `client:` on both.
31. **Coverage collapses in the back half.** Both English-Sub cuts run b-roll only at ~0:05 and ~0:22; from 0:25 to the end (~25 s, half the runtime) it is an unbroken talking head — including the emotional payoff line *"when we go in the classroom where the Mozaik children were playing together"*, which is the most visual line in the piece and has matching gym footage already in the cut. Posted as `b-roll:` on both; both V1s routed.
**Report-only items held consistent across all 23 cuts reviewed 2026-07-30 (do NOT start flagging one of these on a single cut — it is batch-wide or nothing):** (a) the missing French thin space before `?`/`!` (`conflit?` rather than `conflit ?`) — our own posted corrections use the space, but the tracks omit it everywhere; (b) `tu`-form address to the viewer where a cut is otherwise impersonal/*nous* (Keneshbek's close) when there is no internal *tu/vous* contradiction; (c) anglicisms like *se challenger*.
⚠️ **OCR caveat on these cuts:** the white/yellow captions sit on light backgrounds and their **Y position moves between shots**, so Vision drops accents (`où`→`ou`), apostrophes, articles (`la`→`a`) and whole single-word chunks. Confirm every candidate on the crop or a full frame before flagging — 8 candidates were refuted this way in one run.

## 🎯 Goals & Preferences
_The source-of-truth for the typo-qa GOALS & PREFERENCES pillar (3rd review pillar). Consolidated 2026-07-01 from the Context Log; keep dated as new direction lands._
**North-star story angle — default SFCG brand/social:** *"Inspiring, non-generic"* (Kara's explicit tone direction). Avoid NGO-stock tropes. Community-first over pure man-on-street for social (next-phase format = talking-head "living room" vibe; MoS still the historic top performer). Leader series = **multi-partiality** — the whole point is crossing ideological/cultural lines; random picks dilute it. Female VO preferred on the brand video.
**Per-campaign north star — "90 Minutes of Common Ground" (World Cup rail; these Austin cuts belong here):**
- **Tagline / thesis:** "One Game. One Humanity." · *"Conflict is inevitable. Violence is not."* Strategic frame = not "how do we eliminate differences?" but "how do we live, compete, thrive with them?" — football as the proof point.
- **Core MOS question (LOCKED):** *"What has football taught you about people different from you?"* (indirect peace framing — never ask about peace directly).
- **5 content pillars:** Rivalry & Respect · Teamwork Across Difference · Belonging · The World Cup Effect · The Team.
- **Platforms/audience:** IG Reels + YouTube Shorts primary; 18–35 football fans / FIFA WC audiences, social-first. Applies to all legs (Miami / NYC / Dallas / Atlanta / the Austin country-interview series).
- **Pillar-3 read for an Austin country cut:** a cut is ON-TRACK when it uses football to surface common-ground/living-with-difference (opposing teams still find peace, unity through the game, pride across countries) and closes on the SFCG lockup + campaign title; OFF-TRACK if it becomes a generic fan-hype reel with no common-ground/difference beat.
**Hard brand rules (on-screen):**
- SFCG logo + `sfcg.org` CTA only. **NEVER** Preemptive Love / `@preemptivelove` branding (2026-05-12, 3× Frame.io). Only the official "Search for Common Ground" lockup.
- Acronyms **SFCG / CGLA / CGL / "Academy"** are internal-only — never on a super or end card. Program = "Common Ground Leadership Program/Initiative/Community", never "Academy" (retired Mar 2026).
- Proper-noun caps: **"Search for Common Ground"** (capital S, lowercase "for"). A lowercased "search…" on a super is a typo.
- "Shots need narrative context before they read" (2026-05-12) — don't drop a close-up/symbolic image without a setup beat.
**Editing preferences (Rachel Walsh Taza, on-the-record Mar 2 Doha delivery — guardrails for every SFCG cut):**
- **No camera-snapshot / shutter SFX on transitions** (she asked to remove them).
- **Pop-up text with a semi-transparent background over the speaker** — text floats over the speaker, does NOT replace them with a full-frame subtitle screen. *(The Austin cuts use exactly this floating pop-up style — on-preference.)*
- **Smooth cuts, not choppy jumps** — prioritize overlapping B-roll / speech ramps / breath-leave-ins over hard jump cuts.
- **Blue background style approved** for CGL program-leader intros.
- **Screen-recording overlays** (course hub/content) welcomed when they clarify.
- Multilingual captions standard (Arabic/Syria etc.).
- **Conflict-sensitivity (standing, Kara):** politically neutral / multipartial; do-no-harm in sensitive geographies (Palestine/Afghanistan/Haiti — faces-hidden security absolute where flagged); player-led & voluntary, never put words in mouths.
